filename: Comparing Storm Resolving Models and Climates via Unsupervised Machine Learning.pdf
title: Comparing Storm Resolving Models and Climates via Unsupervised Machine Learning
code_availability: Training and postprocessing scripts, as well as saved model weights and python environments, are available on GitHub at DOI:10.5281/zenodo.8024076.
testbed_rationale: The study conducts unsupervised dimensionality reduction, representation learning, and distribution shift analysis across global storm-resolving models and climate states using vertical velocity snapshots, rather than providing training/evaluation datasets for subgrid parameterization or emulation.
pain_points: Massive data volume of global storm-resolving models (nearly 2 petabytes per model for 40 days of hourly output) making analysis and storage a major bottleneck.
Lack of standardized objective methods to compare high-resolution model dynamics and convective organization.
Differences in vertical and horizontal grid structures across various GSRMs requiring interpolation onto standardized grids.
Instability/non-robustness of traditional dimensionality reduction and clustering approaches (raw pixel space, PCA) in high-dimensional turbulent vertical velocity fields.
extraction_notes: The paper uses VAEs and vector quantization (K-means on VAE latent space) to assess distribution shift and KL divergence between GSRMs (DYAMOND) and between +0K and +4K climates in SPCAM. It is funded in part by the NSF LEAP Science and Technology Center (award 2019625).
